summary_rationale: AMD has executed a landmark multi-year business transformation under CEO Lisa Su—growing revenue 8x from $4.32B (FY2016) to $34.64B (FY2025) and $35.17B in 9M 2026 (+44.3% YoY), capturing a record 46.2% x86 server CPU revenue share with EPYC, restoring 40.8% Embedded operating margins, and ramping Helios/Instinct MI450 AI racks across OpenAI, Meta, Oracle, Microsoft, and Anthropic (Q3 2026 Data Center +97% YoY to $8.55B at 33.7% operating margin). However, on a strictly price-blind forensic basis, AMD warrants CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL rather than COMPOUNDER_PASS, with PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health: (1) earnings remain structurally cyclical across PC/Gaming/Embedded and hyperscaler AI capex waves (FY2023 GAAP EBIT fell 89% from its FY2021 peak); (2) 2026 introduced an unprecedented $81.8B off-balance-sheet obligation stack ($48.8B purchase commitments, $13.3B uncommenced DC subleases, $8.5B partner guarantees, $6.2B cloud compute backstops, $5.1B private AI equity commitments) alongside $11.46B inventory (EY Critical Audit Matter); (3) winning multi-gigawatt AI commitments required issuing 320M customer warrant shares (~19.3% potential dilution) alongside $11.1B in November 2026 AI M&A (World Labs $8.2B all-stock + Taalas $2.9B), compressing GAAP ROIC (~5.6%) and elevating dilution risk; and (4) AMD faces a two-front AI squeeze from NVIDIA's CUDA/NVLink ecosystem above and hyperscaler custom ASICs below, plus 22.4% China/HK billing exposure and single-source TSMC leading-edge foundry reliance.
